summary: Feed s158_double to IDS is degraded: 15.6% duplicate packets and 25.5% truncated frames (sliced to ~128 bytes). Slicing breaks full-payload inspection required by IDS, duplicates waste capacity and risk reassembly errors.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding the same packet twice - typically aggregating two SPAN/mirror sessions or two TAP feeds that see the same traffic without deduplication enabled. 586 of 3765 packets (15.6%) exceed 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU processing duplicates, inflates flow/event counts, corrupts TCP stream reassembly and can cause missed detections or false positives.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to drop second copy within short window before delivery to 1Gbps IDS port, ensuring single copy per packet.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has packet slicing/truncation enabled at ~128 bytes to save bandwidth. 959 of 3765 frames (25.5%) are cut short, but this IDS needs_full_payload=true for signature matching.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect application payload beyond L2-L4 headers; payload-based signatures, exploit detection, and file extraction fail, creating major detection blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing for this IDS feed and forward full 1518B frames so IDS receives complete payload for detection; use filtering or load_balance instead of slicing to fit 1Gbps tool port if needed.
